name: Antique Ruby
lede: Antique Ruby is a deep brownish red that the ISCC-NBS system groups with more than twenty other names, from Burnt Lake, recorded as early as 1598, to Hollywood.

sections.title: One block, two dozen names
sections.body:
Wikipedia cites the ISCC-NBS system for this name, which files it in block 13, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates it to 1926 [1]. That single ISCC-NBS block groups over twenty near-duplicate names together: the earliest on record is Burnt Lake, from 1598, and a cluster of others dates to the 1920s, including Brickdust, Chimney Red and Garnet Red [1]. Our sources do not say which of these names was the first in common use, only which dates the library has for each [1].

In LCH terms it measures lightness 29, chroma 48, hue 21 degrees, and the nearest everyday name on file is [[burgundy]], about 3.3 units of ΔE away, a close match [1]. Among named reds it sits beside [[maroon]] and [[red]] itself [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this red in 82 of 23,781 paintings, 0.34 percent, as photographed [2]. The earliest dated match is A Bishop Saint with a Donor, from 1400, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It peaks around 1470, at 9.3 times the archive's overall rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a mid-tone, in 61 percent of its appearances [2].

origin.named_after: undocumented beyond the English words antique and ruby
